Differencing

Edge detection via finite differencing on structured grids.

Computes forward and backward differences at every grid node along each computational direction. Useful for identifying parallel edges whose vertices might intersect between two blocks.

plot3d.differencing.find_face_edges(X: ndarray, Y: ndarray, Z: ndarray)[source]

Compute forward/backward difference vectors on a 2-D face grid.

For each node (p, q) on a face, computes the backward and forward difference vectors along both the P and Q directions. This can be used to check if edges of two faces are parallel (a necessary condition for vertex intersection).

Parameters:

  • X – 2-D array of X coordinates with shape (PMAX, QMAX).

  • Y – 2-D array of Y coordinates with shape (PMAX, QMAX).

  • Z – 2-D array of Z coordinates with shape (PMAX, QMAX).

Returns:

One row per node with columns:

  • p, q – node indices.

  • dp – tuple of backward and forward difference vectors ((dx_b, dy_b, dz_b), (dx_f, dy_f, dz_f)) along the P direction.

  • dq – same for the Q direction.

Boundary differences are zero where no neighbor exists.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

plot3d.differencing.find_edges(X: ndarray, Y: ndarray, Z: ndarray)[source]

Compute forward/backward difference vectors on a 3-D block grid.

For each node (i, j, k) in a block, computes the backward and forward difference vectors along all three computational directions (I, J, K). This is the volumetric analog of find_face_edges().

Parameters:

  • X – 3-D array of X coordinates with shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

  • Y – 3-D array of Y coordinates with shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

  • Z – 3-D array of Z coordinates with shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

Returns:

One row per node with columns:

  • i, j, k – node indices.

  • di – tuple of backward and forward difference vectors ((dx_b, dy_b, dz_b), (dx_f, dy_f, dz_f)) along I.

  • dj – same for J direction.

  • dk – same for K direction.

Boundary differences are zero where no neighbor exists.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame
